 Sources, method and checks
 Sources. The loan master file (LOAN.DAT) gives each loan's terms and current balance. The posting journal (TRANS.DAT) gives every loan transaction from February
 2010 to 9 November 2026. The member master file (BASIC.DAT) gives member numbers and names. LNNAME.DAT and LNTRDESC.DAT give the loan purposes and
 transaction descriptions. Each journal line carries both the member's record and the loan's record, so every transaction is matched to the exact loan it was posted to.
 Balances. The current balance is the balance field on each loan record. One loan was checked against the teller receipt of 9 November 2026: member 1906, GILL,
 MICHAEL KEMAR, 140.00 paid, balance 3,406.13 reducing to 3,281.81. The loan record and journal agree with the receipt exactly.
 Running balances. Each history shows the balance after every transaction, worked backwards from the current balance. As a check, every loan advanced inside the
 journal period should then start from nil. All 109 of 109 such loans do, to the cent. This confirms both the matching and the amounts.
 History before February 2010. The posting journal starts in February 2010. Earlier transactions are shown where the loan record itself still holds them, in a separate
 'Earlier history' table under the loan. For loans already running in February 2010, the first line of the journal history shows the balance brought forward at that date. Older
 loans that closed before 2010 can only show the entries kept on the loan record, which may be incomplete; these are flagged.
 Columns. 'Principal' is principal repaid (credited to the loan). 'Interest' is interest received, with interest refunds shown in brackets. 'Advanced' is new money added to the
 loan, including new loans and refinances. Where a refinance is posted as an advance and a repayment in the same transaction, both are shown and the net effect is
 reflected in the balance.
 Codes. Descriptions come from the system's own code table: Direct Payment, Payroll Deduction, Payment from Shares, Misc. Credit, New Loan, Refinanced Loan, Initial
 Balance, Misc. Debit and so on. Code E has no description in the table and appears on 6 transactions.
 Order. Loans are listed by member number, then loan suffix. The loan account is shown as member number and suffix (for example 1906-A), as on the system's
 receipts. One loan (nil balance) points to a member record that is no longer on file and is shown without a name.
 Recommendation. Reconcile the total outstanding balance to the general ledger loan control accounts (2001 to 2014) before relying on this register.
